commits.message: Markdown draws a rule in -, as Rich's HorizontalRule does (rich-unfiled-791c.x0d0)

Markdown draws a blank row where Rich's new_line puts one (rich-unfiled-791c.mk71) (#437)

* Markdown draws a blank row where Rich's new_line puts one, not one per blank source line (rich-unfiled-791c.mk71)

Rich reads no blank line of the source: every element it exits sets
new_line (a rule and an image clear it), and a blank row goes ahead of
whatever it draws next while it is set. The renderer now walks the
document in Rich's order — images as met, top-level blocks as they exit —
and that flag is the only source of blank rows. Blank tokens and list
item gaps draw nothing; a rule draws its own blank row after it.

Also matches Rich for an empty quote (rich-unfiled-791c.erhp): no row,
and the row its exit puts ahead of the next block.

* Markdown's renderer never sees the block pass's blank and unread marks

They decide only where a container ends; the inline pass now drops them, so
every token the renderer meets is an element Rich exits, and a top-level
block is drawn where its exit is with no per-token test. A list item is its
blocks, without a wrapper.

* Markdown pads an item's and a quote's rows to their width, as Rich's render_lines does

A rule's blank row inside an item was left short of the width, where Rich's
render_lines pads every row of a container's content in its style.

* Markdown's renderTokens keeps its own doc comment above it
